extDescription.message: More keywords for your Firefox address bar: extra search engine keywords, custom search targets, site shortcuts and bundles.

tagline.message: More keywords for your Firefox address bar

statusInvalid.message: Not saved – check the fields marked red

welcomeLead.message: Firefox allows only one keyword per search engine. Barkeys Launcher gives each engine as many extra keywords as you like – and turns any site with a search into a keyword.

featKeywordsText.message: @w, @wiki and @wikipedia all lead to the same search.

featCustomText.message: Any site with a search becomes a keyword via its URL – and site keywords open your favourite pages directly.

featPrivacyText.message: No data collection, no network requests of its own. Your keywords travel with Firefox Sync.

enginesHint.message: Enter extra keywords on the right, separated by commas. Saved automatically.

newEngineIntro.message: You add new search engines in Firefox itself (add-ons aren't allowed to):

newEngineStep1.message: Open Firefox Settings → Search. Add-ons can't open it directly – copy the address and paste it into a new tab (Ctrl+T, Ctrl+V, Enter):

newEngineStep2.message: Under “Search engines” click “Add”: enter name, search URL with %s and the main keyword (e.g. @w)

newEngineStep3.message: Switch back to this tab – the engine appears here automatically

mainNoneTip.message: This engine has no keyword in Firefox. Extra keywords still work; a main keyword (Firefox Settings → Search → pencil) adds the name label.

orphansHint.message: These keywords belong to search engines that don't exist in Firefox on this device – e.g. renamed, deleted or synced from another device. They stay inactive until you assign them or add the engine in Firefox.

customHint.message: Targets by URL, with no Firefox search engine – but without a name label while typing. %s stands for the search terms.

dataSourceHint.message: Enable the search engine that is your Firefox default. Barkeys Launcher spots extra keywords on its result page – it gets access to that and nothing else.

syncText.message: Your keywords live in Firefox's sync storage. With Firefox Sync and “Add-ons” enabled, they're available on all your devices.

syncNoteEngines.message: Note: Firefox doesn't sync custom search engines itself. Add them again on other devices – or use export/import, which can carry their URLs.

backupHint.message: Export your keywords to a file – as a backup, for devices without Sync, or to share. The file stays on your computer.

urlsHint.message: Firefox doesn't tell add-ons the URLs of its search engines. If you enter them here, Barkeys Launcher shows them on import so you can add the engines on a new device.

guideLead.message: Barkeys Launcher doesn't replace your Firefox search engines, it extends them: each engine has one main keyword in Firefox, and in Barkeys Launcher you add as many extra keywords as you like.

guideStep1Title.message: Add the engine in Firefox, with your favourite keyword

guideStep1Text.message: Firefox Settings → Search. Use the keyword you type most often (e.g. @y). Only for that one does Firefox show the engine's name while you type.

guideStep2Title.message: Add extra keywords in Barkeys Launcher

guideStep2Text.message: In the “Search engines” tab, enter e.g. @yt and @youtube. They lead to the same search – handy as a safety net.

guideStep3Text.message: Once, in the “Welcome” or “Data & sync” tab. That's how Barkeys Launcher spots the extra keywords.

guideBarMain.message: Firefox shows “YouTube” right away. You see where you're searching while typing.

guideBarExtra.message: Firefox says “Search with Google”, but after Enter you still land on YouTube.

faq1Q.message: Why doesn't Firefox show the name for extra keywords?

faq1A.message: Add-ons aren't allowed to change the address bar. Barkeys Launcher only steps in after Enter and redirects the search. So the keyword you use most belongs in Firefox as the main keyword – the extra keywords are the add-on.

faq2Q.message: Why do I have to enable my default search?

faq2A.message: When Firefox doesn't know a keyword, it sends the text to your default search. Barkeys Launcher spots the keyword on that result page and redirects before it loads. Barkeys Launcher never sees any other site.

faq3A.message: A keyword without a special character also catches normal searches: with “wiki” as a keyword you can never search for the word “wiki” again. With @ or another character that doesn't happen.

faq4A.message: Yes, via Firefox Sync when “Add-ons” is enabled there. Firefox doesn't sync custom search engines, though – add them on each device. If one is missing, Barkeys Launcher lists its keywords under “Not found in Firefox”.

faq5Q.message: What happens to my data on export?

faq5A.message: The file is only saved locally. Barkeys Launcher sends nothing to the internet. On import every value is checked; invalid entries are dropped.

privacyLead.message: Barkeys Launcher collects no data, has no analytics and makes no network requests of its own. It needs these permissions:

permSearch.message: List your Firefox search engines and search with them

permStorage.message: Save your keywords (via Firefox Sync, if enabled)

permWebRequest.message: Catch the default search's result page and redirect it

permHost.message: Only the result page of the default search you enable – e.g. www.google.com/search. Revocable at any time.

sitesHint.message: A keyword opens a specific site directly – no search. E.g. @news for your news site.

bookmarksPrivacy.message: Bookmark search runs locally in Firefox only. You can revoke the permission anytime in about:addons → Barkeys Launcher → Permissions.

permBookmarks.message: Optional: search bookmarks when you use “Pick from bookmarks” – only asked then.

bundlesHint.message: One keyword opens several sites at once – e.g. @workspace for mail, calendar and project tool. The first site replaces the current tab, the others open next to it.

pickerTitleSite.message: Add a bookmark as a site

pickerTitleBundle.message: Add bookmarks to a bundle (last edited or a new one)

presetsHint.message: Well-known sites with a search. “Add” creates them under “Custom targets” – with the suggested keyword if it's still free. %s stands for your search terms.

presetKeywordTaken.message: Keyword already in use – you'll pick another one when adding

langHint.message: Barkeys Launcher follows Firefox's language automatically. Here you can pick a fixed language for the settings.

faq6Q.message: How do I use a site in several countries or languages?

faq6A.message: Each variant needs its own keyword. A good pattern: the plain keyword for your country, a suffix for the others – dots are allowed. Example: Amazon.de is built into Firefox with @amazon; add amazon.com under “Custom targets” as @amazon.com, English Wikipedia as @wiki.en. The presets suggest such keywords automatically when you pick another country or language in the dropdown.

setupPrivateOff.message: Optional: not active in private windows

setupPrivateOffText.message: Firefox keeps add-ons off there by default, so your keywords don't work in private windows. To allow it: open about:addons → Barkeys Launcher → “Run in Private Windows” → “Allow”.

faq7Q.message: Why don't my keywords work in a private window?

faq7A.message: Firefox only runs add-ons in private windows if you allow it. Open about:addons → Barkeys Launcher and set “Run in Private Windows” to “Allow”. Barkeys Launcher stores nothing from private windows – as always it only reads the search query to spot a keyword.
